headline: Senior military commanders from the U.S., Israel and eight Arab countries secretly met in Germany last week to discuss the war with Iran and the broader regional security situation. Axios reports the meeting, organized by CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper, included the military chiefs of Israel, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Jordan and Egypt. It was the first such gathering since the U.S. and Israel went to war with Iran more than six months ago, and brought together Israeli and Arab military leaders from countries that in some cases still have no diplomatic relations. Cooper reportedly reassured the group that the U.S. will maintain its military presence in the region and briefed them on plans to expand protected shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The meeting also comes as the Houthis escalate attacks on Saudi Arabia and threaten the Bab al-Mandab. Axios reports Israel, Saudi Arabia and CENTCOM are discussing possible Israeli ISR support for Saudi operations against the Houthis. Source: https://www.axios.com/2026/09/15/military-commanders-us-israel-arab-countries-iran-meeting-germany

headline: Video purporting to show the Panama flagged, Qatar owned oil tanker El Gaia with black smoke rising from its superstructure is circulating online following an apparent attack on the vessel near Oman on September 13. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed the tanker struck a naval mine while making what it described as an unauthorized transit. That account has been disputed by U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM), which says the vessel was previously struck by an Iranian missile and was later attacked by an Iranian drone while off the coast of Oman. The available video does not appear to show obvious hull damage consistent with a mine explosion. India’s Ministry of External Affairs confirmed that 13 of the 14 Indian crew members aboard were rescued, with one Indian national remaining missing. Oman has since reported that 23 crew members were evacuated from the tanker, while search operations continue for two missing crew members. The vessel is being towed toward Oman.

headline: The new granite helipad on the White House South Lawn is now complete, paving the way for the U.S. Marine Corps’ VH-92A "Patriot" to routinely operate as "Marine One" from the White House grounds. The VH-92A had seen limited use for White House arrivals and departures because its downward directed exhaust can generate enough heat to scorch or damage the South Lawn. The Marine Corps had therefore continued using the older VH-3D helicopter for South Lawn operations. President Donald J. Trump approved construction of the permanent landing pad, with Sikorsky, the VH-92A manufacturer and a Lockheed Martin subsidiary, providing approximately $5 million to fund the project. The VH-92A is intended to replace the legacy presidential helicopter fleet and provide the president with secure presidential airlift for both routine and contingency operations. This image was posted to President Trump's Truth Social page yesterday.

headline: President Donald J. Trump just made a lengthy post about the U.S. Supreme Court in a Truth Social post this morning, calling several of its recent decisions “horrible,” “destructive,” and potentially devastating to the country. President Trump criticized the Court over rulings involving mail in voting, tariffs and birthright citizenship, arguing that the justices have repeatedly failed to support his administration and accusing some members of being intimidated by Democrats. He specifically praised Justices Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito for dissenting from the Court’s decision on mail in voting, while accusing the broader Court of issuing rulings that could cost the United States “trillions and trillions of dollars” and set the country back “at least a hundred years.” Trump concluded by saying that criticizing the Court would “likely cost me dearly for years to come,” but that he considered it his “obligation and duty” as president to do so.

headline: As part of Operation Economic Outcast against Iran, the U.S. Treasury Office of Foreign Asset Control sanctioned VTB Bank, Russia's second largest bank, under the Iran sanctions program. VTB was already under extensive U.S. sanctions over Russia's war in Ukraine. Treasury now says the bank has helped Iran evade sanctions by establishing relationships with sanctioned Iranian banks, expanding operations in Tehran and creating financial channels for Russia-Iran trade. Treasury also says VTB helped move billions of dollars in frozen Iranian assets.
